```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
devtools::load_all(".")
```

We will begin by creating a `scCNVis` object using the provided example data.

```{r setup}
library(scCNVis)

set.seed(42)

input.matrix <- example.matrix

cell.names <- example.cells

granges <- example.granges

meta.df <- example.meta

#Create a scCNVis object
obj <- scCNVis::createPlotObject(input.matrix, cell.names, granges, meta.df)
```


The scCNVis object is a simple object. It contains the input matrix (accessible
as `obj@Matrix`) and the associated GenomicRanges::GRanges object (accessible as
`obj@GRanges`). It also contains metadata associated with each cell, if provided.

For example, a simple heatmap can be created using the following:

```{r}
#Set custom color scale
heatmap.colors <- c(0,1,2)
names(heatmap.colors) <- c("Blue","White","Red")

heatmap.result <- scCNVis::makeSCHeatmap(obj,
                                         heatmap.colors = heatmap.colors)
print(names(heatmap.result))
print(names(heatmap.result$PlotData))
```

As you can see, the result is a list object that contains the `Plot`, which is
a `ComplexHeatmap` object, and the `PlotData`. In this case, the `PlotData`
is a list containing the actual PlotData (a matrix for the heatmap) and a clustering
result, which relates to the row ordering in the heatmap. In this case, it also
includes the information for drawing the legend of the plot. These values can be used
to create other version of the plot using other packages, or be saved for downstream 
analysis. 

The resulting file can be saved however you would normally export a `ComplexHeatmap`.
For convenience, it can be saved using the scCNVis wrapper function for exporting plots.
The expected output for the heatmap is also shown below.
```{r eval=FALSE}
#Example manual method
#png("output/file.png", width=2000, height=500)
#ComplexHeatmap::draw(heatmap.result$Plot,
#     show_heatmap_legend = FALSE,
#     annotation_legend_list = heatmap.result$PlotData$Legend)
#dev.off()

#Simple wrapper for convenience
scCNVis::saveCustomPlot(heatmap.result, "/path/to/heatmap.png")
```

```{r echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Example 1a. Heatmap", out.width = '100%'}
knitr::include_graphics("1a_heatmap.png")
```

The heatmap can be annotated if metadata has been provided. If needed,
metadata groupings can be added using the `addMetaData()` function. At the same
time, we may choose to limit our plot to specific regions of interest. For this
example, we may choose to exclude chr22, as seen below:

```{r}
plot.regions <- example.granges[example.granges@seqnames != "chr22",]

#If using a basic annotation as shown here and you want to specify colors,
#it should be provided as a named list
#The data here should be consistent with whatever metadata was added to the
#scCNVis object. In this case, our example meta data had 4 subclones. 
#This is optional.
colors <- c("red","blue","green","yellow")
names(colors) <- unique(obj@Meta$Subclone)
annotation.colors <- list(Subclone = colors)

heatmap.result <- scCNVis::makeSCHeatmap(obj,
                                         gr = plot.regions,
                                         annotations = "Subclone",
                                         show.annotation.name = TRUE,
                                         annotation.colors = annotation.colors,
                                         heatmap.colors = heatmap.colors)
#Save the result
#scCNVis::saveCustomPlot(heatmap.result, "/path/to/heatmap.png")
```
```{r echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Example 1b. Heatmap of chr7 and chrX, with sample annotation", out.width = '100%'}
knitr::include_graphics("1b_heatmap.png")
```

To simplify our heatmap, we may wish to present the data as a simple 
average of our subclones, rather than plotting every individual cell in those
subclones. Whenever the heatmap is the result of grouped data, the right side of
the plot will show the number of cells described by each group. 

```{r}

#If using a grouping method, the way to supply annotation colors changes.
#In this case, they can simply be supplied as a character vector
annotation.colors <- c("red","blue","green","yellow")

heatmap.result <- scCNVis::makeSCHeatmap(obj,
                                         group = "Subclone",
                                         annotation.colors = annotation.colors,
                                         heatmap.colors = heatmap.colors)
```
```{r echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Example 1c. Heatmap with pre-specified clusters", out.width = '100%'}
knitr::include_graphics("1c_heatmap.png")
```

`makeSCHeatmap` allows us to identify secondary grouping. For example,
if our data included cells from two samples, we can display what percentage of
our subclones were derived from each sample. Since our example data is all from
a single sample, let us add fake sample labels as metadata and perform secondary
grouping on those fake sample names.

Furthermore, `makeSCHeatmap()` accepts custom functions that can be applied to the plot
data. The custom function should accept an input `data.frame` and return a
`data.frame` with the same dimensions and the same row/column order. Column names
and row names should not be altered. For visual clarity, let's add a function
that changes all values within 1 standard deviation of the mean to be the mean,
so we can focus on whatever strong signals may be present in our data.

```{r}
#Generate fake sample names and add it to our scCNVisObject
ncells <- nrow(obj@Matrix) #number of cells
fake.sample.names <- c("FakeSampleA", "FakeSampleB")
set.seed(42)
fake.samples <- sample(fake.sample.names, size = ncells, replace = TRUE)
obj <- scCNVis::addMetaData(obj, fake.samples, colname = "FakeSampleNames")

#Custom function that takes all values within 1 standard deviation of the mean
#and changes them to the mean, to minimize noise in the heatmap
custom.func <- function(data) {
  sd.value <- sd(data, na.rm = TRUE)
  mean.value <- mean(data, na.rm = TRUE)
  data[data > mean.value - sd.value & data < mean.value + sd.value] <- mean.value
  return(data)
}


heatmap.result <- scCNVis::makeSCHeatmap(obj,
                                         group = "Subclone",
                                         secondary.group = "FakeSampleNames",
                                         post.plot.mod.fun = custom.func,
                                         heatmap.colors = heatmap.colors,
                                         annotation.colors = annotation.colors,
                                         border = TRUE)
```
```{r echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Example 1d. Grouped heatmap with secondary group info", out.width = '100%'}
knitr::include_graphics("1d_heatmap.png")
```
